text:
Philadelphia won 3-1, but Ottawa played the better game. OTT's even-strength expected goals were 1.88 against 0.67 for PHI, and the simulated replays gave the Senators a 56 percent share of deserved wins. The difference was Dan Vladar, who faced 26 shots, stopped 25 and saved 1.33 goals more than the chances against him should have allowed.

Batherson opened the scoring with a snap shot at 5:55 of the second, set up by Claude Giroux and Tim Stützle. PHI answered at 9:03 when Porter Martone tipped one in, with Matvei Michkov assisting. Michkov then scored on the power play at 18:33 of the second, a snap shot that put PHI ahead 2-1. That power play was the home side's best stretch, 1.32 expected goals on three chances, while OTT managed 0.39 on two.

The third period belonged to the Senators, who out-chanced PHI 0.81 to 0.08 in expected goals and still could not tie it. Vladar held, and Trevor Zegras sealed it at 19:46 with a wrist shot, set up by Christian Dvorak and Sean Couturier. Michkov and Martone each finished with a goal and an assist. Ottawa had also lost the earlier meeting on October 8 by 2-1, and this time it generated more and again left without the points.
